variables.name: jChanged
variables.meaning: inserted identities requiring retained or initial extents

assumptions: the collection projection and layout extent owner are canonical
stable identity lookup follows the bounded Core Sequence representation
deterministicWork: one stable-ID lookup per inserted identity
at most one retained extent read or one initial extent creation per inserted identity
contract.resourceRationale: Extent reconciliation allocates only the splice output and one extent entry per inserted identity.
contract.proof: Each inserted identity performs one bounded Sequence lookup and at most one logarithmic extent-index lookup before emitting one extent.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every inserted identity survives from a different retained extent-index leaf or requires a new estimate.

fullScan.rationale: Extent reconciliation must not visit identities outside the inserted change window.

assumptions: one fixed or responsive lane policy is supplied
lane geometry is represented by bounded scalar values
deterministicWork: a bounded number of scalar validation and arithmetic steps
contract.resourceRationale: Lane resolution retains no collection state and allocates one fixed-size result.
contract.proof: Fixed and responsive policies use only scalar validation, division, and clamping.
contract.adversarialWitness: Maximum safe lane counts and finite asymmetric gaps do not increase deterministic work.

fullScan.rationale: Lane resolution has no item domain to traverse.

variables.name: jChanged
variables.meaning: inserted identities plus explicitly changed values

assumptions: the patch is bound to the active projection by an owner-created opaque token
Core Sequence identity lookup has bounded patch depth
deterministicWork: resolver calls equal inserted identities plus the declared value-change range
no unchanged source position is read
contract.resourceRationale: The trusted path retains one bounded Core Sequence patch, changed IDs, and an opaque update token. Scalar rejection occurs before an inserted snapshot is allocated.
contract.proof: Patch creation runs splice-range and resulting-cardinality scalar preflight first, then snapshots and validates only an accepted inserted/value-change range before Core applies one bounded structural patch; token application is constant time.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-083 proves that over-ceiling and out-of-range patches read zero inserted elements and invoke the resolver zero times. Accepted sparse patches retain the existing local identity checks without scanning unchanged values.

fullScan.rationale: A trusted patch must never rediscover unchanged raw-array identity.

assumptions: raw arrays carry no trusted identity patch
the preflight-captured cardinality is the only resolver iteration boundary
deterministicWork: stable input performs exactly nItem ID resolver calls after ceiling validation
callback-induced cardinality drift rejects after at most nItem resolver calls and before resolving appended positions
one Core Sequence construction only after cardinality remains stable
contract.resourceRationale: Initial projection retains the application array reference and one Core Sequence identity owner; callback mutation cannot expand package-owned resolver work beyond the accepted cardinality.
contract.proof: Projection captures the ceiling-validated source size once, resolves only indexes below that bound, and checks the live array length after the fixed resolver loop before Core validates and indexes the resulting stable identities.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-098 starts with one accepted item and a resolver that appends on every invocation; production resolution performs one callback and returns a typed input failure instead of following the moving array boundary.

fullScan.rationale: Initial raw projection must validate every identity.

variables.name: nItem

variables.name: jChanged
variables.meaning: discovered changed window, or nItem when resolver provenance changes

assumptions: unchanged prefix and suffix values preserve object identity
dense Core Sequence repair is O(jChanged) because dense changes make jChanged proportional to nItem
deterministicWork: prefix and suffix comparisons visit at most nItem values
resolver calls and new retained identities are bounded by jChanged
contract.resourceRationale: Raw replacement retains only changed IDs and bounded Core patch metadata unless the changed density makes a full rebuild asymptotically equivalent.
contract.proof: The owner discovers one prefix/suffix window, resolves only that window under stable resolver provenance, and applies one Core Sequence splice.
contract.adversarialWitness: Only the middle item changes after equal prefix and suffix scans consume the rest of a maximum-size array.

fullScan.rationale: Raw arrays provide no patch, so unchanged prefix and suffix discovery may inspect the complete source.

variables.name: jChanged

contract.adversarialWitness: Every value in the declared changed window invalidates a previously exact measurement while all identities outside the window remain untouched.

fullScan.rationale: Value-dependent repair is bounded by the owner-provided changed value window.

contract.proof: Prefix-sum lookup descends the balanced extent index by one branch per level.
contract.adversarialWitness: Lookup at the final offset of a maximum-size non-uniform extent index.

fullScan.rationale: Indexed offset lookup must not visit every extent.

variables.name: jChanged
variables.meaning: distinct retained extents whose final canonical kind/value changes

contract.resourceRationale: Validation canonicalizes the submitted update batch; changed leaves/path nodes are retained only for effective final kind/value changes, while a canonical no-op returns the existing ExtentIndex owner.
contract.proof: Validated updates are sorted/deduplicated once, updateNode descends only paths containing submitted indexes, and unchanged leaf/run entries return their existing nodes so an unchanged root returns the existing ExtentIndex identity.
contract.adversarialWitness: EXT-03/EXT-05 submits same-value and duplicate-index updates whose final canonical value equals the retained extent and proves owner identity is preserved, while estimated(10) to exact(10) produces a distinct owner.

fullScan.rationale: Sparse updates may not scan unrelated extent entries.

contract.proof: Blocked views descend one balanced block path; packed and dense views use direct indexed reads.
contract.adversarialWitness: Read the final item of a maximum-depth blocked owner.

fullScan.rationale: One indexed read cannot visit unrelated blocks.

contract.proof: Iteration visits each retained block and item exactly once without array materialization.
contract.adversarialWitness: Consume a maximum-size view to iterator completion.

fullScan.rationale: Explicit iteration requests the complete logical collection.

contract.proof: toArray allocates one output array and fills each position once from the retained owner.
contract.adversarialWitness: Materialize a maximum-size blocked view.

fullScan.rationale: The explicit snapshot output itself contains every item.

variables.name: nItem

contract.proof: ExtentIndex canonicalizes the measurement batch and path-copies only effective changes. If the canonical root is unchanged, Linear returns the existing layout state before generation publication; changed extent paths and anchor reads remain logarithmic.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-099 submits a non-empty same-kind/same-value batch and proves state/generation identity is retained, then mixes one unchanged and one changed extent and proves exactly one new generation; estimated-to-exact equal geometry remains a real change.

fullScan.rationale: Sparse measurements may not visit unchanged extents.

contract.proof: Gap-aware range search performs bounded logarithmic prefix lookups, then emits each render-window placement once.
contract.adversarialWitness: Non-zero gaps force the nested range search and the viewport emits kPlacement items.

fullScan.rationale: A full visit is permitted only when output kPlacement equals nItem.

assumptions: the extent index proves one canonical uniform run
sequence and extent mutations are owned by their respective indexes
contract.resourceRationale: Formula geometry retains one shared extent and scalar lane geometry regardless of item count.
contract.proof: A uniform extent run derives row count and content extent with scalar arithmetic and stores no per-item masonry placement.
contract.adversarialWitness: Derive geometry for a 100,000-item uniform masonry domain and assert that no placement is copied, recomputed, or retained.

fullScan.rationale: Uniform geometry is independent of the mutation position and cannot scan the unchanged domain.

variables.name: cCandidate
variables.meaning: uniform row and lane candidates intersecting scalar query bounds

assumptions: the extent index proves one canonical uniform run
sequence patch depth is capped at 32
deterministicWork: one scalar row-bound calculation per visible lane
visited item indexes equal render candidates
only emitted placements enter the domain-order sort
contract.resourceRationale: The query allocates only the render-window placement output and retains no query cache.
contract.proof: Closed-form row bounds skip the offscreen domain, each candidate is visited once, and only emitted placements are sorted back into domain order.
contract.adversarialWitness: Query a narrow render window near the end of a maximum-size uniform domain and count only emitted placements.

fullScan.rationale: A bounded render window cannot visit unrelated offscreen items.

contract.proof: ExtentIndex canonicalizes the measurement batch first. An unchanged canonical owner returns the existing Masonry state before generation or placement publication; an effective change path-copies extent paths and may cascade lane placement recomputation from the first changed item.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-099 proves a non-empty same-kind/same-value batch retains state/generation, while an estimated-to-exact transition remains a real change; changing the first effective item under balanced shortest-lane placement can still reflow every later item.

fullScan.rationale: Cascading shortest-lane ownership can make every later placement observably change.

assumptions: the normalized geometry changes laneCount, itemGap, or placementPolicy
the materialized shortest-lane heap path is bounded by maxLanes

contract.proof: Changing laneCount, itemGap, or placementPolicy routes through buildInternals without a retained owner; each materialized item is placed once and shortest-lane selection uses the existing bounded lane scan/heap strategy.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-097 changes each packing input independently and verifies a fresh logical owner with all materialized placements recomputed and equivalent to a fresh rebuild.

variables.name: nItem
variables.meaning: masonry item count whose logical packing is retained

assumptions: domain and extents are unchanged
laneCount, itemGap, and placementPolicy are unchanged
contract.resourceRationale: Exact no-ops allocate no replacement Masonry state/placement owner; projection-only changes allocate one state wrapper while retaining the existing logical placement/lane internals.

Axis, flow, laneExtent, and laneGap changes reuse the retained MasonryInternals because placement lane/start/extent data does not depend on those projection fields.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-097 exercises exact omitted/explicit no-ops and isolated axis, flow, laneExtent, and laneGap changes on a 4,096-item materialized owner with stable state or retained internals identity and unchanged deterministic Masonry work counters; the benchmark holds geometry delta fixed while nItem grows from 1k to 100k.

fullScan.rationale: No-op and projection-only geometry mutations may not enumerate or rebuild logical placements.

contract.adversarialWitness: Every visible lane contributes interleaved placements requiring the output sort.

variables.name: nTrack

contract.adversarialWitness: Regions span pinned and center partitions so every partition query returns duplicate/interleaved candidates.

variables.name: nTrack
variables.meaning: retained partitioned row and column track count

assumptions: the active track owners and identity maps are canonical
partition groups are retained as contiguous ranges
contract.resourceRationale: Region-only replacement retains all track owners and allocates only canonical replacement regions plus their delegated Track Grid region indexes.

fullScan.rationale: Region-only replacement may scan the changed region set but must not enumerate the retained track domain.

contract.adversarialWitness: A dense measurement, a boundary-shrinking removal, or a saturated structural overlay forces the selected rebuild branch.

contract.proof: Scalar splice range/cardinality preflight runs before any inserted Spatial item is read; accepted declaration order is retained by the bounded Sequence patch chain while changed geometry is copied into a bounded owner-local overlay; order-only patches retain the packed tree unchanged.

assumptions: the active Spatial state and retained indexes are canonical
the Core Sequence delta remains below its own materialization crossover
the Spatial repair remains below its packed-tree or structural-overlay rebuild crossover
contract.resourceRationale: Existing-ID updates reuse blocked-vector/packed-tree repair. Membership changes patch only declared Sequence identities and retain removed/new/changed geometry in the bounded structural overlay.
contract.proof: Each declared upsert is captured once. Membership-preserving changes enter applySpatialBaseChanges or the existing overlay repair. Structural updates remove only declared IDs from the retained Sequence, append only new upsert IDs, and pass removed/new/changed geometry to applySpatialOverlayChanges; unchanged Spatial items and packed-tree leaves are not enumerated.

Dense membership-preserving value changes likewise reuse applySpatialBaseChanges' existing rebuild crossover.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-095 adds enough new IDs to exceed the structural overlay bound and verifies one rebuild containing the complete resulting domain.

fullScan.rationale: A full scan is allowed only after a documented Sequence or Spatial owner crossover selects rebuild.

contract.resourceRationale: Sparse construction retains one canonical region/index entry per accepted region; column-start search and row-end ordering are construction-only auxiliary state.
